tasks.short: Assist engineers developing photonic products and processes

steps.what: Assist engineers in developing products, fixtures, tools and processes through practical technical work

tasks.design: Retain practical development assistance with the technician. Use {OTHER}, optical design and test tools, and drawings in {DOCS} as part of that work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on physical behaviour and evolving engineering requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing design tools support development without replacing practical assistance.
tasks.still_hard: Diagnosing unfamiliar behaviour and translating an engineer's idea into a workable fixture or process.
tasks.human_edge: The technician notices practical constraints and tests ideas with the engineer.

reach.task: Explain performance objectives and development constraints
reach.learn: Which practical observations change the design direction

evidence.claim: Practical photonics development assistance is not replaced by the digest's drafting or report capabilities.

assumptions: Boundary is practical assistance on new products, fixtures, tools or processes; separate formal reporting is excluded.
Engineer supplies objectives and drawings; technician produces observations and technical contributions during s1. No ready performance or feasibility flags are assumed.
Use existing design and test tools first.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new development automation is proposed.
unknowns: Development activities actually assigned to technicians
research_questions: Which development delays require physical experiments rather than document generation?

already_counted.description: Practical technical assistance and engineering discussion

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Practical development is retained in full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend optical design or material improvements

steps.what: Assess optical equipment design or material alternatives against cost, time and performance evidence
Recommend optical equipment design or material changes and explain the technical trade-offs

tasks.design: Keep alternative assessment and the recommendation with the technician. Use {DOCS} sources and {OTHER}, optical analysis tools, to support the trade-off discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reducing cost or processing time must preserve the required optical performance.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing analytical tools can support comparisons without deciding which change is technically acceptable.
tasks.still_hard: Material compatibility, tolerances, yield and unintended performance consequences.
tasks.human_edge: The technician connects practical production observations to the proposed design change.

evidence.claim: Optical design-change recommendations require contextual technical judgement; no distinct clerical saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is assessing and recommending changes, not approving a design release or performing the resulting experiments.

Production staff and purchasing records supply observed times and costs; technician verifies units, material grades and performance constraints in s1. No free compatible-material or equivalent-performance flags are assumed.
Use existing optical analysis capability first; its runtime is not a human saving.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new comparison engine or data feed is introduced.
research_questions: Which proposed changes need physical evidence before a recommendation can be made?

already_counted.description: Technical alternative assessment and recommendation discussion

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60+40=100; zero gross and net saving. Technical assessment and discussion retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor inventory and order required supplies

steps.what: Monitor inventory, reconcile physical stock and verify supply requirements and reorder parameters
Calculate replenishment quantities and draft supply orders using checked catalogue references
Check supply specifications, resolve exceptions and place the exact required order

tasks.design: Configure {ERP} replenishment calculations and draft orders in {PROCUREMENT} from checked stock and parameters. Keep physical reconciliation, technical specification checks and order placement with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock balances, actual demand and supplier pack sizes need to agree before replenishment can be calculated.
tasks.enabler_now: Native inventory and purchasing configuration can calculate and populate repeat orders.
tasks.still_hard: Special optical specifications, unreliable stock records, changed demand and unavailable items.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises whether a supply is actually suitable for the intended work.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time calculating and copying routine replenishment orders.

reach.task: Confirm catalogue items and supplier conditions

evidence.claim: Native inventory rules can calculate draft replenishment from verified stock and parameters; suitability and order approval remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring supplies and ordering, not receiving delivery or carrying out optical work.

Technician physically verifies item, location, usable quantity, reserved quantity and unit in s1, then checks demand, minimum and target stock, pack conversion, lead time and catalogue specification. The technician produces those exact reorder parameters in the same counted step; they are not a free par-level input.

Buyer and supplier provide catalogue identifiers, pack sizes and terms; s1 includes checking and mapping them. Missing stock, parameters or specification stops s2 for manual calculation and buyer discussion in s3.
Test native inventory configuration first; existing automated replenishment runtime earns no labour saving and no unreviewed substitutions are permitted.
research_questions: Can native draft replenishment reduce calculation and copying after physical checks and parameter upkeep are counted?

already_counted.description: Physical reconciliation, parameter capture and exact order checks

incremental.description: Maintain reorder parameters and review changing technical supply requirements
Maintain catalogue mappings and inventory configuration

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, catalogue item and specification, quantity, unit, price, delivery location and date; changes require renewed checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+0+25=70; gross 30 minus focal upkeep 8 gives net 22 in an E1 scenario. Range 0-5 allows existing replenishment, small order volumes and frequent specification changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Optimise photonic parameters through physical device trials

steps.what: Make prototype or production devices and optimise photonic process parameters from observed performance

tasks.design: Retain physical device-making and parameter assessment with the technician. Use {OTHER}, process-control and measurement tools, and the trial plan in {DOCS} during the experiments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Parameter optimisation depends on actual manufactured devices and observed performance.
tasks.enabler_now: Current measurement and process tools support the trials without replacing them.
tasks.still_hard: Process interactions, repeatability, yield and attributing a change to the correct cause.
tasks.human_edge: The technician responds to physical behaviour and recognises when another trial is needed.
tasks.altitude: Experimental work and technical responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.task: Set trial objectives and permitted parameter limits
reach.learn: Which evidence would justify a parameter change

evidence.claim: Making photonic devices and assessing physical performance is not replaced by a dashboard or report generator.

assumptions: Boundary is physical parameter trials, not a separate report or design-recommendation task. Development-assistance roll-ups must assign overlapping trial work once.

Engineer supplies the trial plan and limits; technician produces actual settings, device identifiers and measured observations during s1. No ready optimum-parameter or successful-trial flag is assumed.
Use existing process and measurement tools first; machine runtime is not human effort.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new experimental automation is proposed.
research_questions: Which parameter decisions need more physical evidence rather than another display of existing results?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Physical trials and interpretation retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce routine replenishment paperwork while retaining practical photonics development and trials.
reach: Check technical catalogue specifications with buyers
role.ambitious_version: A technician with reliable supply replenishment who keeps time for physical development, technical judgement and experiments.
